memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now the family heads of the Levites approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the other tribal families of Israel at Shiloh in Canaan and said to them, "The Lord commanded through Moses that you give us towns to live in, with pasturelands for our livestock." — Josh 21:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Every other tribe had received a portion of land, but the Levites had none — and that was by God's own design. The Lord had told them long ago that He Himself would be their inheritance (Numbers 18:20). So here the Levites come forward, not grabbing territory, but humbly asking for what God had already promised through Moses: towns to live in and pasture for their animals.

Notice how they ask. They do not demand. They simply remind the leaders of what the Lord had commanded. There is a quiet confidence here — the confidence of people who know that God keeps His word, and that His promises are worth waiting for.

The Levites remind us that our security is not finally in what we own but in the God we belong to. For the believer today, this points forward beautifully. In Christ, God says that He is our portion, our treasure, our inheritance (Eph 1:11-14). We may hold very little in this world, yet if we have Him, we have everything that lasts.

When you feel you have been given less than others, remember the Levites. The Lord who was their inheritance is your inheritance too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to measure your security by what you own or by whom you belong to?
2. How does it change your outlook to call God Himself your inheritance?
3. Are there promises of God you can wait for with quiet confidence today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You Yourself are my inheritance and my portion. Teach me to hold this world loosely and to treasure You above all things. Amen.
